The same-runtime ghost (NVS RESTORE_REQUIRED, RAM clear) is not an INV-BOOT-MIRROR violation: only boots are judged, and this trace has no reboot after the ghost. Severity: availability / cost (low-medium) plus diagnostics: an R1 single-owner design-rule breach in the same runtime (two durable obligations on 256-261); no unsafe write in any probed chain: the ghost START wrote nothing, a reboot inside the admitted lease meets PR41's dual lockout (export contained at 244 = 2, operator needed: F-FW01-2), a reboot after it restores or stops at OPERATOR DECISION REQUIRED. Reachability: INFERRED: a single-key commit false negative on the Phase-B marker itself. ESPHome 2026.8.2 sync() clears its whole pending queue and the data commit's sync runs just before in the same lambda, so the 'unrelated pending key' route cannot reach this commit; the remaining route is ESP-IDF ESP_ERR_NVS_REMOVE_FAILED (the new value is written, the old entry's erase fails), which needs a flash-operation failure and an old marker entry (any device that completed a lease before: PB-01-a starts with one); then a second START (owner or HA schedule) before any reboot; rate UNKNOWN. The first lease makes the marker key hold CLEAR, the precondition of the ESP-IDF REMOVE_FAILED route (the property also finds the never-used form, seed 69).
